A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same preference-leakage study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, added, and removed content to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original student-model training experiments, Arena-Hard and AlpacaEval 2.0 evaluations, human annotations, and leakage and recognition analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds model-size evaluations, pairwise student recognition, and an original analysis of leaderboard ranking differences.

M1.justification: The synthetic-data generation and student-training pipeline, SFT/DPO/ICL procedures, and BERT response classifier remain unchanged. The additional model configurations and recognition format extend evaluation rather than introduce a proposed training method or model component.

E1.justification: Core training sources and Arena-Hard/AlpacaEval 2.0 coverage remain. v2 adds a quantitative scenario comparing Chatbot Arena and AlpacaEval rankings for their shared model population (Section 5.4), while removing v1's MTBench LLaMA-2 human/GPT-4 comparison. The preliminary MTBench inspection remains in Appendix A.

E2.justification: v2 Table 4 introduces an explicit egocentric-bias comparator: GPT-4 Preview is contrasted with preference leakage affecting Vicuna 7B/13B/33B. v1's MTBench GPT-4/human comparisons involving LLaMA-2, Claude-v1, and other models disappear. The main GPT-4o/Gemini/LLaMA judge set and SFT/DPO/ICL comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds a size study covering Qwen-2.5 3B/7B/14B and Qwen-3 1.7B/4B/8B/14B (Figure 4a), pairwise recognition alongside pointwise recognition (Table 5), and a cross-leaderboard ranking-difference protocol (Table 4). Existing training settings and the BERT 80/20 split remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses directly test model-size sensitivity and real-world ranking effects relative to egocentric bias. Recognition analysis is expanded to test identification from paired responses. The MTBench analysis explaining GPT-4's preference for LLaMA students is removed; data-mixing, relatedness, learning-method, category, and human-annotation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports model-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The three-annotator protocol, majority voting, and reported agreement of 78.6 remain unchanged in Appendix B.3.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes the Mistral GPT-4o/LLaMA-3.3 Arena-Hard score from -6.7% to -1.5% and its average from -2.7% to -0.1%; Figures 2 and 3 are unchanged. Recognition entries of 60.0/25.4/54.2% are replaced by pointwise results of 41.0/53.2/41.8%, with new pairwise results of 52.0/44.2/29.8%, respectively for GPT-4o/Gemini/LLaMA. BERT remains at 82.4%. Model-size results and ranking differences of 1.00 for egocentric bias versus 1.33 for preference leakage are added, while MTBench results are removed.

T1.justification: Section 3 replaces v1's model-set-overlap formulation with generator/student output distributions, judge scoring functions, and an expected-score inequality comparing related and unrelated judges with comparable assessment capabilities. Inheritance is expanded formally to include direct fine-tuning and output distillation, and family relatedness explicitly incorporates shared architecture and training data. These revise the central definitions; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The conclusion reverses the model-size claim from greater bias in larger students to greater bias in smaller students, and emphasizes question types instead of comparable model pairs. RQ2 and the conclusion also explicitly include real-world impact analysis. The central claim that preference leakage is pervasive and difficult to detect remains.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the larger-model memorization explanation with a hypothesis that smaller models learn recurring spurious features. It adds benchmark-difficulty explanations and interprets leaderboard differences as evidence that preference leakage can exceed egocentric bias. The GPT-4-to-LLaMA inherited-bias explanation is removed. Appendix B.3 nevertheless retains the earlier statement about greater leakage in more powerful students.

D1.justification: New Appendix D identifies the models included in the leaderboard comparison, and Appendix E supplies the added pairwise recognition prompt. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, BERT implementation settings, and code/data access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands the focused comparison with egocentric/self-preference bias, adding works such as Liu et al., Wataoka et al., and Chen et al. (2025), and adds Wadhwa et al. on distillation tracing. Hayes et al. supports the revised DPO interpretation, while several references accompanying the earlier preliminary discussion are dropped. The overall positioning as related-model contamination remains.

P1.justification: Section 3 is substantially rewritten and reorganized into oracle usage, formal definition, and relatedness types. Further Analysis is reordered, main-result discussion is revised, human-annotation discussion moves to Appendix B.3, and the impact statement moves to Appendix G. Author-date citations become numbered citations.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two columns to one, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. v2 Figure 4 combines a new model-size panel with the retained data-mixing plot; the MTBench plot disappears and the human-annotation plot moves to the appendix. A leaderboard table is added, and the recognition table gains separate pointwise and pairwise columns.

improvement.justification: The clearer central definition, corrected PLS indexing and Table 1 values, and within-Qwen size comparisons improve precision and evidence beyond v1's cross-family size inference. These are useful but limited gains: Appendix B.3 retains an unreconciled larger-model interpretation, and the new leaderboard analysis attributes cross-benchmark ranking differences to bias without isolating alternative explanations.
